data.name: The Adventures of Tree
data.detailed_description:
The Adventures of Tree takes you on an open-ended adventure to save your fellow species from the evil invaders; Florps!

Throughout this cute and charming hand-drawn game, you will have to make choices that will impact your story and eventual game ending while being free to roam the open world and vast landscapes, searching for epic treasures, and fighting all sorts of different creatures and bosses along the way!

Keep yourself laughing as you interact with the quirky and comical dialogue while completing a massive variety of different quests and missions to guide your way.

With countless hours of gameplay, huge replayability, and over 100 different achievements, this is not a game you want to miss out on!

reviews.review:
[h1][b][u]First 1.5 Hours Impressions[/u][/b][/h1]

[i]So I played for an hour and a half and kept notes on what I was experiencing and things I liked and didn't like, I figured I'd share these notes with you (the developer) for some quick hints on how to patch up next, and how a new player like myself may experience your game (which hopefully gives you a good idea how to make future changes). This is mostly for the developer, but if you're thinking of purchasing this game go ahead and read through my notes. Warning: this will be length, but hopefully helpful.[/i]


[h1]Gameplay Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*]very professional-feeling intro
[*]upgrading stats is cool, I like the design
[*]i got three-shot by a porcupine 10 minutes into game, this better not be one of those games where the difficulty is ALL over the place. i was too tall to hit him
[*]i really like how this looks like a much less serious and concrete game from the outside, but it does indeed have basically all the features most RPG's have
[*]the Minecraft-styled Furnace is a neat touch
[*]dialogue is pretty funny
[*]my only complaint as of yet is the combat, it's very loose and sometimes (like the porcupine) downright unfair, how do i hit him? he's too damn short (edit: I think I figured it out, he's not killable, just jump over him...)
[*]i love quests, don't get me wrong, i actually love the grindy ones where you just collect a few things and return, but i feel like i got bombarded with quests immediately, that may overwhelm some players
[*]day-night cycle was unexpected and very cool
[*]immedaitely noticed how the inventory is too small, especially with 10 different collect quests at a time
[*]it'd be nice if the movement was a bit quicker, seeing as there's lots of backtracking to be done, or maybe if sprint regenerated faster; at this rate i'll be wasting Upgrade Points on speed (edit: upgraded map negates backtracking nicely)
[*]some of the quests consist of just waiting and picking the twigs once they respawn, since I'm not strong enough to explore anywhere else
[*]the fast travel options make the slow walking speed much more bearable
[*]the stat page should pause the game, I'm fine with the map or inventory being open while the game is playing but the stat page should be safe
[*]why don't the boars fight back?
[*]should've been a sign pointing left from my house, I thought I could only go right (I may just be stupid, too). once you go left THEN this game gets like twice as good, now that there's a village and tons of merchants right next to my house
[*]lots of content, tons of items, expected much less. still just wish the combat was better: maybe it would've worked better if it were turn-based instead
[*]game progresses extremely slowly; might turn new players away
[*]chests should have an "auto-deposit" type of feature, where you can just stack all the like items in your inventory onto the corresponding ones in the chest
[*]NOTE TO NEW PLAYERS: the game starts extremely slow, once it gets going though it's a lot of fun and much more fleshed out than you may have originally thought!
[/list]

[h1]Aesthetic Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*]awesome narrator
[*]button clicks are annoying and too loud
[*]axe sound is weird, especially considering i'm only hitting air. also too loud
[*]so far, i actually really like the child-like art style
[*]some interactable background objects are hard to distinguish from the rest of the background, I find myself spamming E as I walk around to make sure I didn't miss anything
[*]the setting and mood of the game is heartwarming; it's lovely
[*]while I adore the art-style, I feel like it causes the gameplay to be more clunky
[/list]

[h1]Technical Nptes[/h1]
[list]
[*]no 1920x1080 support?
[*]clicking should be able to be used to interact as well, like click an object to pick it up; since we're given the choice between using UP or LMB to attack, why not let us use the mouse for more?
[*]BUG: in the first shop you come across, the info box for the Wooden Sword got stuck on my cursor even after i closed the shop, wouldn't go away until I re-opened the shop and hovered over any other item
[*]BUG: the tooltip box didn't come up for Garlic a couple times while hovering over it
[*]you should be able to auto-equip items with RMB
[*]BUG: "Bottle of Poison" doesn't have an icon, the tooltip box just appears whenever I hover over the empty inventory slot
[*]map should close after you've just fast-travelled
[*]BUG: got another tooltip box stuck on my cursor by opening my inventory while inside a shop
[*]you can hurt yourself by throwing a Tomahawk at a wall you're touching?
[*]weapons should have an actually helpful tooltip, like the fact that once you throw a Tomahawk you have to actually go pick it up, basically rendering it useless in a game with this style of combat
[*]why is W sleep? shouldn't it be interact and not considered a door, and use E instead? guess it doesn't really matter
[*]people with completed quests should have some stereotypical way of showing the player; like an exclamation point over their heads; I get so many quests at once I have no idea who asked for what (or they could be waving to get your attention: if you want a cuter way to do it than an ugly exclamation point)
[*]why doesn't my character on the start menu have his equipped items?
[*]the auto-save spots should be more emphasized, I'm not sure what saves and what doesn't; all I know is my bed does, but I've also started in the middle of the city once but without the items I got right after leaving it. to my knowledge the center of cities and your bed are the only things that save??
[*]the "Hello there! I'm the law around these parts." lady should only say that once, instead of every single time you hit E near her
[/list]


[i]Overall, this is a pretty solid and very promising game. It's a good experience but I'm worried people may be turned away too early in the game before they get to experience it for real. To fix this major issue I'd just like to see the game start up a bit quicker, explain some things more, and just re-do the combat completely; the combat is seriously my only ACTUAL real problem with this game. It just doesn't work, at least this early in the game. And I'm not saying it's too difficult, I just mean it's ridiculous when you're slowly swinging a hatchet that does 1/10 of the enemy's health, while they're bumrushing you and jumping all over and hitting for like 1/5 of your health every second. It gets a bit frustrating but offers a nice challenge which is good. I hope to see this game improve consistently and I'm looking forward to the complete version! Hope I helped, and have a great day![/i]
